newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Unisource unit launches European ATM backbone net.
newsitem.headline: Unisource unit launches European ATM backbone net.

text.p: Unisource Carrier Services, a unit of Unisource NV, said it had launched an ATM Backbone Network among Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Geneva, London, Madrid and Stockholm.

The network uses asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) technology to handle several international services and applications -- such as high-speed voice, data, Internet and video -- over the same centrally controlled network, it said in a statement.
"A further extension of this ATM-based service platform to Paris, Milan, the United States and other major business centres is scheduled for later this year," it said.
A large part of the capacity is reserved for fast-growing Internet traffic, it said, but any combination of services can be implemeted.
UCS has also introduced a new service called Internet Transit, it said. It gives service providers access to European and trans-Atlantic networks.

"This is a major enhancement to our portfolio of earlier services. We believe that ATM will play an increasingly important role for our carrier customers," said Ray Pritchard, UCS director of products and services.

Unisource partners PTT Telecom of the Netherlands, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT announced earlier this month they would merge their international networks into UCS, creating a $2 billion a year business employing 900 people.
The launch of the pan-European ATM network is not related to this because it does not involve building up infrastructure in shareholder countries, a UCS spokesman said.

"This is something that we have developed ourselves on a European basis," he added. "But it gives our shareholders and other potential customers the opportunity to use ATM not just up to the border, but in Europe." -- Zurich newsroom +41 1 631 7340
